title: Reminders: after a switch to another record, the old record's last good read stands in for a failed read before the permission ask, so it could vouch for the new record's erase
evidence: Done: fixed by PR 1608, as defence in depth: no path to the switch-down case is known (connect merges the phone up, a reopen merges the phone's file in, Disconnect copies down; adversary on PR 1608). From the owner's review of PR 1597. ios/HealthRoadmap/Reminders/ReminderScheduler.swift kept lastEpoch, the last good read, through a switch between phone and cloud records, and ReminderMode.swift asking x asked uses it when the read as the ask began fails. Switch down: record A read at epoch 5; a switch to record B (epoch 1); B's read before the ask fails; B is erased to epoch 2 while iOS answers; the grant compared A's 5 with B's 2 and would turn reminders on for the erased record (US-11). Switch up: record A read at epoch 0; a switch to record B at epoch 3 whose read before the ask fails; the grant compared A's 0 with B's 3 and ended off, as an erase would (fails safe, S40). Fix: RootView calls ReminderScheduler.recordSourceChanged() when the source or the cloud's open changes (a connected cloud shows the phone's copy until it opens); it clears lastEpoch and bumps a generation token. A refresh begun before the switch never writes lastEpoch, and an ask that spans a switch drops both reads taken before it. With no good read of the new record the grant ends off, and the next tap after a good read turns reminders on. Pins (_US25_AC12b): switch down; switch up and back; a good read after a switch restores the fallback; the window before the cloud opens; a refresh in flight across a switch; a switch during the ask. Not pinned: RootView's trigger itself (checked by reading), and where the store swaps the shown text after the connection changes (a re-sign-in while open, closeFailed, keepFailed), a refresh in between can still read the old text under the new token until the next good read or open (adversary on PR 1608, no real path found). US-25 AC12b Follow-up (owner's checkpoint review): CloudSync.open sets the session (recordOpen) before RecordStore.draw awaits the engine and swaps the record, so a refresh in that gap read the phone's copy under the open's token and could become the fallback; with the tap's read failed and a remote erase during the ask, the phone copy's higher epoch could vouch for the grant. Fix: RootView's reminders trigger now keys on the whole ShownRecord (source, open, erase epoch shown), so the draw that moves the epoch bumps the token too; one onChange calls both recordSourceChanged and recordChanged. A store swap that keeps the epoch leaves a fallback of the same value. An ask in flight when the draw moves the epoch now ends off (fail safe; the next tap turns reminders on). The key is ShownRecord.switches (moved from RootView to Reminders/ReminderScheduler.swift), pinned by the table test testWhichChangesToTheShownRecordEndTheLastGoodRead_US25_AC12b, which fails for PR 1608's key (epoch left out); RootView's onChange calling it is checked by reading. Contract test: testARefreshBetweenTheOpenAndTheDrawNeverVouchesForTheCloudRecord_US25_AC12b drives the scheduler as RootView now does. Residue (adversary): the key watches the drawn epoch while the scheduler reads the record text, so a swap between two undrawn records (a failed screen, then a held remote erase) does not bump the token; it also needs the cloud's epoch below the phone's, with no known path.
